title: Applied labs
description: Build, break, debug and evaluate in your own environment.

lessons.title: Lab: Requirements, gateways & serving
lessons.conceptOverview: Design a 100K-user assistant. State active-user fraction, requests per user, input/output tokens and peak multiplier before choosing capacity.
lessons.whyItMatters: Design a production AI platform from requirements to recovery.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Translate users into request rate, token rate and concurrency using workload assumptions. Gateways enforce authentication, tenant quotas and model routing. Queues absorb bursts but add waiting time; streaming reduces perceived delay without reducing total generation work. GPU scheduling must account for prefill and decoding workloads.

sections.title: 1. Establish a baseline
sections.content: Write down your inputs, expected behavior and constraints before starting. Design a 100K-user assistant. State active-user fraction, requests per user, input/output tokens and peak multiplier before choosing capacity.

sections.title: 2. Introduce a failure
sections.content: Test the mistaken assumption: Registered-user count alone determines GPU capacity. Record the observed result and the point where it diverges from your prediction.

sections.title: 3. Debug and evaluate
sections.content: Use the mechanism to explain the failure: Translate users into request rate, token rate and concurrency using workload assumptions. Gateways enforce authentication, tenant quotas and model routing. Queues absorb bursts but add waiting time; streaming reduces perceived delay without reducing total generation work. GPU scheduling must account for prefill and decoding workloads. Change one variable at a time. Repeat the baseline and add a held-out case. Submit the implementation, results and limitations.

commonMistakes: Registered-user count alone determines GPU capacity.
keyTakeaways: Translate users into request rate, token rate and concurrency using workload assumptions.

lessons.title: Lab: Retrieval, caching & tenancy
lessons.conceptOverview: Draw an enterprise RAG architecture. Trace one request across authentication, retrieval, generation and audit logging, including every tenant boundary.
lessons.whyItMatters: Design a production AI platform from requirements to recovery.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: A production RAG service includes ingestion, object storage, metadata databases, vector indexes and authorization-aware retrieval. Cache keys need model/version, prompt and tenant scope. Semantic caches can return inappropriate answers if similarity ignores permissions or freshness. Rate limits and backpressure protect shared resources.

lessons.title: Lab: Reliability, cost & capstones
lessons.conceptOverview: Design a ChatGPT-style platform for ten million registered users. Include a cost model, load test, regional failure drill and rollout/rollback plan.
lessons.whyItMatters: Design a production AI platform from requirements to recovery.
lessons.engineerDeepDive: Define availability targets, recovery time and acceptable data loss. Observe latency percentiles, errors, token usage and queue depth. Capacity planning uses measured throughput at the target latency. Failover may change model behavior, so fallback quality needs testing alongside infrastructure recovery.
